newsitem.title: UK: Granada rules out bid for Yorkshire.
newsitem.headline: Granada rules out bid for Yorkshire.

text.p: Granada Group Plc said on Thursday it had no current intention of bidding for ITV neighbour Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc.

"Granada confirms that, unless there is a material change in Yorkshire's circumstances (including an offer from a third party), it has no current intention of making an offer for Yorkshire," the company said in a statement.
Granada has taken advantage of a relaxation of UK media ownership to build up a total stake of around 27 percent in Yorkshire and a full bid has long been anticipated.

Yorkshire chairman Ward Thomas said this week that a takeover bid for his company should be pitched as high as 17 pounds per share. Yorkshire shares dived after the Granada statement, plunging 175p to 1105p.

"The board of Granada believes that the current Yorkshire share price already reflects not only a significant bid premium caused by continuing speculation, but also an expectation of a substantial reduction in Yorkshire's annual licence bid payment, realisation of which is far from certain," the statement added.
"Reports of the possibility of Granada making an offer for Yorkshire at or above the current market share price are misplaced," Granada added in its statement.
United News & Media Plc, which operates ITV franchises for southern and eastern England, has a stake of some 14 percent in Yorkshire and is another potential predator.

Bid speculation has helped to fuel a rise of more than 80 percent in Yorkshire's share price over the last 14 months and the company was valued at in excess of 800 million pounds before the Granada statement. Yorkshire chairman Thomas conceded this week that a bid from Granada was "extremely likely".
Yorkshire this week announced a 40 percent rise in annual pre-tax profit to 30.2 million pounds.

But Thomas said this would be greatly enhanced if Yorkshire could negotiate a reduction in the annual licence fee of 66 million pounds which it pays to the Treasury. Any new rate would take effect from 1999.
